title: Record the characteristic polynomial of A_1 on the 80-dimensional isotypic summand
body:
<!-- CURSOR_AGENT_PR_BODY_BEGIN -->
## Change and mathematical scope

Exact proof over `Q` of the characteristic polynomial of `A_1` on the 80-dimensional isotypic summand inside the trivial-character `(+1,+1)` joint space of the historical `c=1` centre block.

The summand is the image of the projector for the linear character `ψ(r^k)=(-1)^k`, `ψ(r^k u)=(-1)^k` of the dihedral group generated by the signed permutations `r` and `u` recorded in PR #7023. On an explicit basis its characteristic polynomial is

```text
chi_{A_1}(x) = x^10 (x-2)^3 (x+2)^3 (x-6)^2 (x+6)^2 f14(x) f14(-x) f16(x) f16(-x).
```

Here `f14` and `f16` are the multiplicity-one degree-14 factor and the degree-16 factor of the published degree-216 polynomial:

```text
f14(x) = x^14 - 14x^13 - 180x^12 + 2824x^11 + 10112x^10 - 202144x^9
         - 173568x^8 + 6293376x^7 - 97024x^6 - 86923264x^5 + 8403968x^4
         + 453709824x^3 + 132964352x^2 - 739049472x - 498401280
f16(x) = x^16 + 12x^15 - 180x^14 - 2344x^13 + 11488x^12 + 173824x^11
         - 277632x^10 - 6136576x^9 - 321280x^8 + 105269248x^7
         + 108563456x^6 - 773404672x^5 - 1259880448x^4 + 1656389632x^3
         + 3560341504x^2 - 112656384x - 1702232064.
```

The same basis splits the summand into two `A_1`-invariant subspaces of dimension 40, with polynomials

```text
x^6 (x-2)^2 (x+2)^2 (x-6) (x+6) f14(x) f14(-x)
x^4 (x-2) (x+2) (x-6) (x+6) f16(x) f16(-x).
```

Algebraic multiplicity of eigenvalue 0 is 10. The geometric multiplicity is not computed. No new kappa. The selected conditional kappa stays `781451/250000000`.

Evidence class: a proof by exact finite linear algebra over `Q`. The domain is the full image of one explicit projector. It is not a heuristic search, and it is not an exhaustive census of the `c=1` stabilizer.

## Task and overlap

- Task: `formal-interface-lemma`, scope changed.
- Upstream base: `17469fff78c22941280f04d39dc5a1faee09c840`.
- Predecessor: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7023
- Question this answers: open question 1 of that PR, recorded at https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19514162
- Package: `research/a1-isotypic-80-charpoly/`

The catalogue card asks for a formal caller binding. PR #7023 proved the opposite linear character's 8-dimensional summand reducible and recorded that this character has projector rank 80, without a basis or a polynomial. This package builds that basis and the matrix of `B = 4 A_1`.

Overlap on 2026-11-10: 339 open PRs and 7013 discussion records, pagination complete; local notes 10180, HEAD paths 10178, complete. The phrases `80-dimensional isotypic` and `multiplicity-80` matched only #7023. This package does not redo that 8-dimensional reducibility result, the degree-216 characteristic polynomial of #6964, the 8-dimensional joint spaces of the 32-dimensional `c=1` sign character, or the 128-dimensional isotypic component.

## Validation

CPython 3.12.3, standard library only.

```sh
python3 -B -W error research/a1-isotypic-80-charpoly/verify.py
python3 -B -O research/a1-isotypic-80-charpoly/verify.py
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/a1-isotypic-80-charpoly --check-only
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/a1-isotypic-80-charpoly
```

Marker: `PASS_A1_ISOTYPIC_80_CHARPOLY`. Both modes passed. Metadata check returned `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS`. Registered replay returned `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`. Selected baseline returned `PASS_RESEARCH_BASELINE_BINDINGS_ONLY`.

The projector satisfies `(12P)^2 = 12(12P)`, has trace 960 and rank 80, and the 80 orbit vectors are fixed by `12P`. On that basis `r` acts by `-I` and `u` acts by `+I`. The matrix of `B` has entries in `-48..48`. Its characteristic polynomial is lifted by the Chinese remainder theorem from the Hessenberg recurrence, with a prime product larger than twice the Gershgorin binomial bound, and it agrees with determinant interpolation modulo the first prime. The displayed factors multiply back to `chi_{A_1}`, and the degree-14 and degree-16 factors are irreducible by the Rabin test. Ascending coefficients of `chi_{A_1}` have SHA256 `bd72312859b05d7cd69c5cc94e4768998cd033869ab9f157fdf9d2042b6bc0d2`.

Rejection controls cover a coordinate transposition, the incomplete swap of coordinates 4 and 7, a swapped port label, a nearby change of `r`, a dropped orbit term, the trivial character of the same dihedral image, and a one-entry matrix change.

Not run: Lean, Docker, the degree-881 replay, the degree-216 characteristic polynomial, and the selected cold replay.

## Credit

Prepared by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok assistance.

JoyboyBrian recorded the sign-character dimensions. PR #6944 split the trivial `c=1` character into 216-dimensional blocks. PR #6964 pinned the basis and the characteristic polynomial of one 216-space. PR #7008 named `r` and `u` and the dimensions 8, 80 and 128. PR #7023 proved the 8-dimensional summand reducible and left this polynomial open. Ali Romman's PR4958 and PR4720 retain the query and the Bell action. Krzysztof Wojt's `research/exact-one-slot-gram/` supplies the degree-881 annihilator. Nick Petalas's PR5120 is the degree-410 lower bound. The doubled representation comes from PR1719. New work is Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

See `research/a1-isotypic-80-charpoly/TASK.json`.

- What is the geometric multiplicity of eigenvalue 0 of `A_1` on this summand? The algebraic multiplicity is 10. The pinned matrix of `B` has not been row-reduced.
- What is the characteristic polynomial of `A_1` on the 128-dimensional isotypic component of the two-dimensional rational representation of this same dihedral image? That remains open question 2 of PR #7023. The degree-136 quotient of the published degree-216 polynomial by this polynomial still contains the 8-dimensional summand, so it is not that 128-dimensional polynomial.
